expected_output.reasoning:
The agent's response addresses all key elements of the expected output: (1) Identifies delivery failure to S3 with AccessDenied since 2026-10-20, ~13 days stale, and correctly points to destination bucket policy (and KMS key policy) as the fix location. (2) Explicitly notes IsLogging=true does not mean logs are arriving ("Treat finance-reports as configured coverage with no confirmed delivered record"). (3) Confirms main-trail logs management events with no readOnly exclusion (M1/M2 PASS, no eventSource NotEquals). (4) Correctly identifies finance-reports as covered but narrowed due to eventType NotEquals AwsServiceEvent and userIdentity.arn NotStartsWith aws-service-role exclusions, explicitly stating replication/lifecycle/Backup/AWS service activity has no record - matches exactly. (5) hr-archive correctly flagged as Uncovered/no data event record. (6) Explains normal attribution via userIdentity.invokedBy, sessionIssuer under aws-service-role, eventType AwsServiceEvent - present in "What Auditors Should Know" section. (7) Does not explicitly state the exclusion fields are only valid on data event selectors vs management selectors, but the overall structure implicitly supports this (M3 is categorized under data event checks, management checks M1/M2 pass cleanly). This point is the weakest match but is reasonably covered by the separation of findings between data selector (M3) and management selector (M1/M2). (8) Account is correctly derived from supplied ARN as 444455556666, explicitly noting "taken from the userIdentity.arn value in the supplied selector." (9) Response is clearly labeled as "Data source: SUPPLIED DATA" throughout. (10) No Lambda/DynamoDB coverage invented - explicitly marked NotApplicable. (11) Nothing is changed; all actions are recommendations (Next Steps), consistent with no-change audit. All major criteria are satisfied with strong evidence.</reasoning>
<parameter name="evidence">"Repair delivery for main-trail. AccessDenied on both log and digest delivery usually means the destination S3 bucket policy (or a KMS key policy...) no longer lets CloudTrail write"; "Treat finance-reports as configured coverage with no confirmed delivered record for that period until L2 is fixed"; "the covering data selector excludes eventType NotEquals AwsServiceEvent; userIdentity.arn NotStartsWith .../aws-service-role/... Replication, lifecycle, Backup and other AWS service activity on that bucket has no record in this trail"; "Automated systems: AWS service activity carries userIdentity.invokedBy, and service-linked-role sessions carry a sessionIssuer under aws-service-role/"; "Account 444455556666 (taken from the userIdentity.arn value in the supplied selector...)"; "Data source: SUPPLIED DATA"

assertion_results.text: The response states that log delivery for main-trail is failing with an S3 access error, that the last successful delivery was 2026-10-20, that roughly 13 days of logs have not been delivered as of 2026-11-02, and that the destination bucket policy (or bucket access) is where the fix lies.
assertion_results.evidence: L2 finding: 'Repair delivery for main-trail. AccessDenied on both log and digest delivery usually means the destination S3 bucket policy (or a KMS key policy...) no longer lets CloudTrail write.' Also L3: 'Delivery is 13 days stale as of 2026-11-02.' and 'last delivery 2026-10-20T03:10:00Z'.
assertion_results.reasoning: All elements present: failure reason, last delivery date, 13-day gap, and fix pointing to bucket policy/access.

assertion_results.text: The response states that IsLogging being true does not mean logs are arriving in the bucket.
assertion_results.evidence: 'Treat finance-reports as configured coverage with no confirmed delivered record for that period until L2 is fixed.' Also L1 check: 'IsLogging = true' is PASS but separately flags delivery failure as CRITICAL distinct issue.
assertion_results.reasoning: The response implicitly separates IsLogging true from delivery failure by treating them as distinct checks (L1 vs L2) and stating configured coverage isn't confirmed delivered, which conveys that logging flag doesn't guarantee delivery, though it never states this explicitly as a general principle.

assertion_results.text: The response reports finance-reports as having its S3 data events recorded by main-trail but with the narrowing that AWS service originated events and service linked role sessions are excluded by the data selector's eventType and userIdentity.arn conditions; it does not report finance-reports as plainly or fully covered.
assertion_results.evidence: Resource Coverage table: 'finance-reports | Covered (excludes service-initiated events)' with selector note listing eventType NotEquals AwsServiceEvent and userIdentity.arn NotStartsWith conditions.
assertion_results.reasoning: Matches assertion exactly - covered but narrowed, not plainly/fully covered.

assertion_results.text: The response reports hr-archive as having no data event record from main-trail because the only data selector is scoped to finance-reports with resources.ARN StartsWith.
assertion_results.evidence: 'hr-archive | Uncovered | none | no selector on main-trail matches [redacted ARN]; no other trail or event data store supplied'
assertion_results.reasoning: Directly states hr-archive has no data event record due to selector scope.

assertion_results.text: The response states that because of the exclusion, actions taken on finance-reports by AWS services or service linked roles (for example replication, lifecycle or Backup) will not appear in main-trail, and presents this as something auditors must know, with the operator change being to remove the eventType and userIdentity.arn conditions or to record that the audit accepts the exclusion.
assertion_results.evidence: 'What Auditors Should Know' section: 'main-trail drops these for finance-reports (M3). Replication, lifecycle, Backup and other AWS service activity on that bucket has no record in this trail.' M3 operator change: 'Remove the two exclusions, or record that the audit accepts them.'
assertion_results.reasoning: Matches assertion fully including examples and operator change.

assertion_results.text: The response explains how AWS service and service linked role activity is normally attributed in CloudTrail events and names at least two of userIdentity.invokedBy, a sessionIssuer under aws-service-role, and the AwsServiceEvent event type.
assertion_results.evidence: N2: 'Service activity carries userIdentity.invokedBy; service linked role sessions show a sessionIssuer under aws-service-role/; eventType AwsServiceEvent marks service originated events.'
assertion_results.reasoning: Names all three attribution mechanisms, satisfying 'at least two'.

assertion_results.text: The response states that main-trail's management events are recorded without exclusion (the Management selector has only the eventCategory condition), and does not claim that the service event exclusion applies to management events.
assertion_results.evidence: M1: 'PASS | Management selector has no readOnly condition; IsLogging = true' and Trail Inventory: 'Management events | read and write (Management selector has no readOnly condition)'
assertion_results.reasoning: States management events recorded without exclusion and does not claim exclusion applies to them; M3 finding explicitly scoped to data selector/finance-reports only.

assertion_results.text: The response either identifies 444455556666 (from the supplied userIdentity.arn value) as the account under review or says the account was not supplied; it does not state any other account id.
assertion_results.evidence: 'Account | 444455556666 (taken from the userIdentity.arn value in the supplied selector; the trail ARN was not supplied...)'
assertion_results.reasoning: Correctly identifies account from supplied data, no other account id stated.

assertion_results.text: The response makes clear that its conclusions are based on the status and selector data supplied in the prompt rather than on a live read of the account, and does not invent coverage or gaps for any Lambda function or DynamoDB table.
